conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 A. Xylem (Water-Conducting Complex Tissue)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Angiosperms have vessels + tracheids; Gymnosperms have tracheids only (except Gnetales). Stems have Endarch xylem; Roots have Exarch xylem.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
XYLEM ELEMENTS
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                         ▼                         ▼
     TRACHEIDS                 VESSELS / TRACHEAE       XYLEM PARENCHYMA & FIBERS
 (Imperforate, tapered)       (Perforated end-plates)  ├── Parenchyma: Living, storage
 ├── Pitted / Bordered pits   ├── Continuous tubes      └── Fibers: Dead, lignified
 └── Gymnosperms & Ferns      └── Angiosperms only          mechanical support
conceptBreakdown.content:
Xylem conducts water and mineral nutrients unidirectionally from roots to aerial parts and provides rigid mechanical support.

### Primary Xylem Elements
1. **Tracheids**: Elongated, tube-like dead cells with thick, lignified walls and tapering, imperforate ends. Water moves between tracheids laterally through **Bordered Pits**. Primary water-conducting element in Gymnosperms and Pteridophytes.
2. **Vessels (Tracheae)**: Long cylindrical structures formed by a vertical series of dead cells (vessel members) joined end-to-end. End walls feature **Perforation Plates** (simple or scalariform). Vessels are diagnostic of **Angiosperms** (*ABSENT in Gymnosperms, except Gnetales: Gnetum, Ephedra, Welwitschia*).
3. **Primary Xylem Ontogeny**:
   - **Protoxylem**: First-formed primary xylem with narrow tracheary elements (annular or spiral thickenings).
   - **Metaxylem**: Later-formed primary xylem with broader tracheary elements (reticulate or pitted thickenings).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Protoxylem Arrangement: Endarch vs. Exarch
conceptBreakdown.title: Protoxylem Arrangement: Endarch vs. Exarch
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PROTOXYLEM ARRANGEMENT PATTERNS
                      
      ENDARCH ARCHITECTURE (Stems)              EXARCH ARCHITECTURE (Roots)
      
      Periphery ──► Metaxylem                   Periphery ──► Protoxylem
      Center    ──► Protoxylem                  Center    ──► Metaxylem
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Endarch Arrangement (Stems)**: Protoxylem lies toward the center (pith), Metaxylem lies toward the periphery. Development occurs **centrifugally** (inside $\rightarrow$ outside).
• **Exarch Arrangement (Roots)**: Protoxylem lies toward the periphery, Metaxylem lies toward the center. Development occurs **centripetally** (outside $\rightarrow$ inside).

conceptBreakdown.content:
Phloem transports organic solutes (sucrose, amino acids) bidirectionally from source to sink.

### Primary Phloem Elements
1. **Sieve Tube Elements**: Long, tube-like, living cells arranged vertically. End walls are perforated by sieve pores to form **Sieve Plates**.
   - **Enucleate State**: Mature sieve tube elements lack a nucleus, vacuole tonoplast, and ribosomes, but remain living due to functional metabolic regulation by adjacent **Companion Cells**.
   - **Phloem Protein (P-Protein) & Callose**: P-protein and carbohydrate callose form plugs at sieve plates upon injury to seal the phloem and prevent nutrient leakage.
2. **Companion Cells**: Specialized parenchymatous cells ontogenetically derived from the same mother cell as their adjacent sieve tube element. Connected via dense **plasmodesmata**; they maintain the pressure gradient across sieve tubes.
   - *Gymnosperm Equivalence*: Gymnosperms lack true companion cells and sieve tubes; they possess **Albuminous Cells (Strasburger cells)** and **Sieve Cells**.
3. **Phloem Parenchyma**: Absent in most Monocotyledons.
4. **Phloem Fibers (Bast Fibers)**: Sclerenchymatous dead fibers providing mechanical support; commercially harvested from *Corchorus* (Jute), *Linum* (Flax), and *Cannabis* (Hemp).
